newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power flat to lower on mild weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power flat to lower on mild weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the western U.S. remained soft amid mild weather conditions and surplus supplies, trade sources said Wednesday.
"The weather forecast is for slightly above-normal temperatures. It's going to be soft for a while," said a California trader.
A utility trader in Montana predicted warmer temperatures and consequent spring runoff will put a cap on prices for the rest of this month, and possibly through June, as hydropower output increases.
Snowpack in the Northwest ranges between 130 and 200 percent of normal levels for this time of year, while California snowpack averages more than 140 percent of normal.
Due to the abundant hydropower, the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear unit in Washington will run at 55 percent capacity until further notice, a spokesman said Wednesday.
Also on the supply side, the 1,221 MW unit 3 at the Palo Verde nuclear plant near Wintersburg, Arizona, was expected to be completely off-line by Saturday for a scheduled 50-day refueling outage.

The 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear plant in southern California was expected to restart sometime during the last week of February after being shut for maintenance and refueling on November 30.
The Pacific Northwest was expected to see near normal temperatures through Thursday, followed by slightly above normal for Friday and the weekend, Weather Services Corp said.
The Southwest was expected to see above normal temperatures Thursday through Sunday.
Firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) for Thursday was quoted at $10.00-$11.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), little changed from Wednesday.
Firm, off-peak COB deliveries for Thursday were also steady at $6.50-7.50.
Firm, peak electricity at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) for Thursday was slightly lower at $9.00-9.75.
Off-peak Mid-C for day-ahead delivery was quoted at $6.00-7.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was marginally weaker at $12.25-13.00.
Off-peak PV was quoted flat at $7.00-8.00.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $12.00-13.00, while off-peak was at $6.50-7.50.
